name: Austria

findings.summary: Nokia won a multi-year contract to supply A1's 5G radio access (AirScale) and 5G core in Austria; in January 2026 A1 again named Nokia as its 5G partner.
findings.analyst_inference: Nokia (Finnish) is third pole. Value and duration undisclosed. ORF reports Huawei and ZTE components are also present in A1's network without saying where; that residual role is not coded. A1 is majority-owned by America Movil (Mexico), which does not change the equipment-vendor pole.

findings.summary: ZTE is Drei Austria's long-standing network equipment supplier and partner for its 5G rollout, from the 2019 Linz launch through upgrading all sites to 5G and work on 5G standalone in 2022.
findings.analyst_inference: Tier 5 because Drei's 5G network is operational nationally with ZTE as named equipment supplier; the 2022 RCR piece is ZTE-sponsored and treated as S4, so corroboration rests on SDxCentral, RCR 2019 and ORF. No source states ZTE's exact RAN/core share; ORF (2026) says Drei uses both ZTE and Huawei components. still_current null: no explicit 2026 confirmation of ZTE as main vendor beyond ORF's statement that ZTE components are in use.

findings.summary: Magenta's 4G network was built by Huawei under its T-Mobile Austria name; for 5G it uses Nokia, Ericsson and Cisco and reportedly still Huawei, while saying its core is free of Chinese vendors.
findings.analyst_inference: Single opened S3 source; tier 5 reflects the operational Huawei-built 4G RAN. Date is the reporting date, not the original build. Whether Huawei RAN is being replaced, and Huawei's 5G share, are unknown. Nokia/Ericsson/Cisco 5G role not coded separately.

findings.controller: Austrian Scientific Computing consortium (TU Wien lead)
findings.local_actor: TU Wien, University of Innsbruck, JKU Linz and partner universities
findings.financier: EU Recovery and Resilience Facility / Quantum Austria / Austrian science ministry
findings.summary: MUSICA, Austria's national research supercomputer across Vienna, Innsbruck and Linz (45.11 petaflops), run by the TU Wien-led Austrian Scientific Computing consortium, was officially inaugurated on 3 July 2026 after phased operation from 2025.
findings.analyst_inference: Owner-operator is a domestic public university consortium, so domestic. TU Wien cites EUR 36m investment funded by the EU Recovery and Resilience Facility, Quantum Austria and the science ministry; not converted. Lenovo (hardware) and MEGWARE (storage) are IT suppliers, not civil builders. Inauguration date per Interesting Engineering (day not independently checked).

findings.summary: MUSICA uses Nvidia H100 GPUs (four per node, roughly 1,088 in total across three sites) with AMD EPYC CPUs, supplied in Lenovo hardware.
findings.analyst_inference: GPU total: TU Wien's node counts (112+80+80 nodes x 4) give 1,088, matching Interesting Engineering. CPUs from AMD (also US). No export-licence issue expected for an EU state.

findings.controller: Advanced Computing Austria (ACA) GmbH consortium, hosted at TU Wien
findings.local_actor: AIT Austrian Institute of Technology, TU Wien and partners
findings.financier: EuroHPC Joint Undertaking / Republic of Austria
findings.summary: AI Factory Austria (AI:AT), an EuroHPC-backed project led by ACA with TU Wien hosting, began in July 2025 with a EUR 30m project budget; reporting cites EUR 80m overall, mostly for 650-700 GPUs.
findings.analyst_inference: Tier 3: EU grant agreement in force (CORDIS: start 1 July 2025, total cost EUR ~30m, EU share ~EUR 15m); the EUR 80m (EU 40m / Austria 40m) figure from Trending Topics covers hardware procurement. GPU vendor not named and procurement not confirmed, so no silicon finding. Values not converted.

findings.summary: Austria began rolling out GovGPT to federal ministries in July 2026, aiming at over 180,000 federal staff; it runs on the federal computing centre's AI infrastructure, currently using a Mistral AI model with no provider data access.
findings.analyst_inference: Coded domestic because the model runs on BRZ servers and the provider is said to have no data access, implying self-hosted weights; the government release does not name Mistral (trend. does). Exact Mistral model and licence unknown. Tier 4 = production rollout begun ministry by ministry, not yet at full scale. Provider described as swappable.

applications.null_reason: one search found no Austrian Hikvision/Dahua removal, safe-city procurement or foreign-stack e-government AI beyond GovGPT (coded under models)

power.null_reason: no AI- or data-centre-specific power project surfaced in facilities searches
